title: An Employee record that checks itself

blocks.text: A record may customise what it generates: validate in a compact constructor, override `toString`, and add methods of its own.
Complete `record Employee(String name, int id, LocalDate hireDate)`:

items: **compact constructor**: a `null` name is refused with a `NullPointerException` whose message is `Name cannot be null`; a `null` hire date with a `NullPointerException` whose message is `Hire date cannot be null`; an `id` of 0 or less with an `IllegalArgumentException` whose message is `ID must be positive` (`Objects.requireNonNull(value, message)` helps);
**`boolean isNewHire(LocalDate today)`**: `true` when the hire date is strictly after the date six months before `today`.

blocks.text:
new Employee("Alice Smith", 4, LocalDate.of(2023, 4, 1)).toString()
        -> "Employee(name=Alice Smith, id=4, hired on 2023-04-01)"
new Employee(null, 1, date)       -> NullPointerException: Name cannot be null
new Employee("Test", 0, date)     -> IllegalArgumentException: ID must be positive
new Employee("Test", 1, null)     -> NullPointerException: Hire date cannot be null

today = 2023-08-22
hired 2023-05-01 -> isNewHire(today) = true
hired 2022-01-01 -> isNewHire(today) = false
hired 2023-02-22 -> isNewHire(today) = false   (exactly six months)

cases.says: A valid employee keeps its components and prints as Employee(name=Alice Smith, id=4, hired on 2023-04-01).
A null name or hire date is refused with NullPointerException and its own message.
An id of 0 or below is refused with IllegalArgumentException('ID must be positive').
Someone hired exactly six months before today is no longer a new hire.

concepts: A record can still validate in a compact constructor, override toString and add methods of its own.
